content.title: KITCHEN MISTAKES THAT QUIETLY MAKE YOUR FOOD {{DANGEROUS}}
facts: **Garlic-in-oil** – Don't store homemade garlic oil at room temperature (low-oxygen environment can let Clostridium botulinum grow).
**Chicken** – Don't rinse raw chicken under the tap before cooking (splashes spread Salmonella/Campylobacter around your sink and counters).
**Potatoes** – Don't eat ones that have turned green or sprouted (solanine builds up and can cause nausea at higher levels).
**Eggs** – Don't store them on the fridge door (temperature swings there speed up bacterial growth compared to the colder interior shelves).
**Melon** – Don't leave cut melon out for hours before refrigerating (its moist, low-acid flesh is a prime spot for Listeria and Salmonella).
**Mushrooms** – Don't keep them sealed in plastic bags (trapped moisture speeds up mold growth; paper bags let them breathe).
**Leftover pasta/rice sauces** – Don't cool them slowly on the counter overnight (the long cooldown window lets Bacillus cereus spores multiply).
**Reheated spinach** – Don't reheat it more than once (repeated heating raises nitrite levels, especially risky for infants).
**Canned food** – Don't use a dented or bulging can (swelling can signal gas from bacterial contamination inside).

caption:
A few of these kitchen habits are way more common than people realize. Take garlic oil: when raw garlic sits in oil at room temperature, it creates a low-oxygen pocket that's exactly what Clostridium botulinum spores need to grow and produce toxin, so it has to stay refrigerated and get used quickly. Potatoes are another sneaky one — once they turn green or start sprouting, solanine levels climb, and that compound is what's behind the nausea and stomach upset some people get after eating old spuds. And that habit of rinsing raw chicken? It feels hygienic, but the water splashing off the meat can carry Salmonella or Campylobacter up to a meter across your sink, counters, and nearby dish towels. Everyone's kitchen setup is different, so just double check the habits that apply to yours.
